title: Signed event delivery (HTTPS transport binding)
description: How one canonical event envelope (envelope.schema.json) is carried over HTTPS from a producing engine to a consuming service, and how the consumer acknowledges it (docs/architecture/signed-event-delivery.md). The event is the contract; this is only one transport for it. The same envelope may later travel over a broker without change.

keyId.description: Identifies the delivery key the sender signed with. The consumer looks the key up in its own configuration; the key id carries no secret and no authority beyond that lookup.

timestamp.description: The sender's clock at signing, UTC, whole seconds, RFC 3339 with a literal Z. Signed again on every delivery attempt, so a retry is never rejected as stale merely because the first attempt was long ago.

signature.description: <algorithm>=<lowercase hex>. Only hmac-sha256 is defined; the algorithm prefix is how a stronger scheme (asymmetric keys, workload identity) is introduced without changing the headers.

DeliveryHeaders.description: The three signature headers. The body is the exact bytes of one envelope, Content-Type application/cloudevents+json, at most 1 MiB. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over the UTF-8 string  baobab-event-delivery-v1 LF <recipient> LF <key id> LF <timestamp> LF <lowercase hex SHA-256 of the body>  (LF = 0x0A, no trailing LF), keyed with the key's secret of at least 32 random bytes. <recipient> is the consumer's fixed service name (baobab-control-plane), so a signature made for one consumer is worthless at another.

DeliveryReceiptAccepted.description: The 202 answer: the first receipt of this (source, id), durably recorded.

DeliveryReceiptDuplicate.description: The 200 answer: a redelivery of a (source, id) already accepted with identical content.

DeliveryReceipt.description: A 2xx answer means the event has been durably accepted (recorded), never that it has been acted on. ACCEPTED is the first receipt of this (source, id) (202); DUPLICATE is a redelivery of an event already accepted with identical content (200). Each answer has its own schema below, so status cannot contradict the HTTP status. A sender treats both as delivered.

SenderPolicy.description: Documented, machine-checked constants. Delivery is at-least-once: a sender retries until it receives a 2xx, a consumer deduplicates by the envelope's (source, id), the delivery identity envelope.schema.json defines. Replay window and retention are minimums a consumer must honour, and the retry horizon is a maximum a sender must honour.

max_retry_horizon_hours.description: A sender stops retrying an event, and dead-letters it, at most this long after its first attempt. It must stay below receipt retention, so a retry can never arrive after the consumer has forgotten the first acceptance and be taken for a new event. Re-publishing a dead letter later is a new delivery; applying an event is gated on its revision, so a late duplicate is harmless.

permanent_failure_statuses.description: A sender dead-letters at once on these (a retry cannot change the answer); any other non-2xx is retried with backoff up to its attempt limit and then dead-lettered.
